signature: SUBROUTINE DGEEV( JOBVL, JOBVR, N, A, LDA, WR, WI, VL, LDVL, VR,

params.name: jobvl
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: left eigenvectors of A are not computed;
-   `= 'V'`: left eigenvectors of A are computed.

params.name: jobvr
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: right eigenvectors of A are not computed;
-   `= 'V'`: right eigenvectors of A are computed.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten.
params.workDependent: the real Schur form T is unique only up to rotations of its 2-by-2 blocks and signs, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: WI
params.reference: `WR` and `WI` contain the real and imaginary parts, respectively, of the computed eigenvalues. Complex conjugate pairs of eigenvalues appear consecutively with the eigenvalue having the positive imaginary part first.

params.name: VL
params.reference: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVL = 'N'`, `VL` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$.
params.workDependent: each left eigenvector is unique only up to sign, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: ldvl
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array `VL`. $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge 1$; if `JOBVL = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge N$.

params.name: VR
params.reference: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVR = 'N'`, `VR` is not referenced. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) + i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j) - i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$.
params.workDependent: each right eigenvector is unique only up to sign, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: ldvr
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array `VR`. $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge 1$; if `JOBVR = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge N$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,3 \, N)$, and if `JOBVL = 'V'` or `JOBVR = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge 4 \, N$. For good performance, `LWORK` must generally be larger.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues, and no eigenvectors have been computed; elements i+1:N of `WR` and `WI` contain eigenvalues which have converged.

untranslated: WORK.minLength: local MINWRK is assigned inside nested control flow

overrides.reason: DGEEV hands its LWORK to DGEHRD, DORGHR, DHSEQR and DTREVC3, which pick their block size, AED window or back-transformation from LWORK. The blocked and unblocked Hessenberg reductions round differently, and the QR iteration that follows can then reach a different real Schur form T (2-by-2 blocks rotated, rows and columns of other signs) with eigenvectors of the opposite sign; past the reference's crossover the eigenvalue order changes too. The reference does this as well: compiled LAPACK 3.12.0 DGEEV at N = 150 and 200 (random matrix, JOBVR = 'V') returns a different A, a different order of WR, and VR entries of different magnitude at LWORK = 4N than at its queried optimum. The JS dgehrd crosses over at NX = 32 where ILAENV(3) gives 128, so the JS path changes from N > 33 (the reference's from N > 128). The eigenvalues do not depend on LWORK beyond rounding at the sizes the tests reach; the module's tests check them, and the eigenvector residual, at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (ticket 0100).

set.params.A.workDependent: the real Schur form T is unique only up to rotations of its 2-by-2 blocks and signs, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
set.params.VL.workDependent: each left eigenvector is unique only up to sign, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
set.params.VR.workDependent: each right eigenvector is unique only up to sign, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
